sentences.show: On the morning of 12 June 1962, a guard at Alcatraz tried to wake a prisoner. His head rolled onto the floor.
It was fake. Soap, toilet paper, and real hair from the prison barbershop.
Three men were gone. Frank Morris, and the brothers John and Clarence Anglin.
Alcatraz was meant to be escape-proof. A rock, in the freezing currents of San Francisco Bay.
For six months, they dug through the walls under their sinks, with spoons, and a drill made from a vacuum cleaner.
Morris played the accordion during music hour, to cover the noise.
On the empty top floor of the cell block, they built a raft from more than fifty stolen raincoats.
On the night of 11 June, they climbed to the roof, slid down a pipe, and got over two fences.
A fourth man was left behind. His hole was too small.
At about 10 p.m., the three pushed their raft into the dark bay. And vanished.
Searchers found a paddle, a life vest, and a wallet wrapped in plastic. Never the men.
The FBI decided they drowned. Their family says they made it to Brazil.
In 2013, police got a letter signed "John Anglin", saying he was still alive. It was never proven.
And in 2025, a team rebuilt their raft from the same plans, and made it across.
So did they drown in the bay? Or pull off the perfect escape?
Three men vanished. Don't you vanish. Subscribe for the next escape.
